name: Southwest Face
approach: From Trinity Trailhead (2,800 ft) at the end of Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200, follow the Buck Creek Trail (#1513) roughly 9-9.5 miles, climbing through forest, an old avalanche debris field (~4,500 ft), and past an unmarked junction with the Pass No Pass way-trail (bears right, ~5,800 ft). Continue up the way-trail to Pass No Pass (~6,400 ft) and the alpine camping benches beyond, from which Fortress's southwest face and south ridge come into view. Note: since 2026, storm damage has closed FR 6200 to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground (about mile 16), adding roughly 7 miles of road-walking…
firstResearcherNote: Parties camp in the basin below Pass No Pass or at Buck Creek Pass; both added. Elevation of the Pass No Pass basin camp not confirmed, so omitted.

camps.name: Basin below Pass No Pass
camps.notes: The small basin reached by the unmarked way trail that leaves the Buck Creek trail about a mile below Buck Creek Pass. The closest camp to the southwest face; the scramble starts above it.

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass
camps.notes: The popular camp at the top of the Buck Creek trail, roughly ten miles from Trinity. From here drop back down the trail about a mile to the Pass No Pass way trail.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds

name: Southeast Slopes
approach: From the end of FR-5606 (the North Fork Entiat Trailhead, ~3,940 ft), pick up the North Fork Entiat River Trail #1437. This lower section sits outside wilderness, so mountain bikes are legal and commonly used to knock out easy miles. The first ~6 miles follow the North Fork Entiat River on a gentle, mostly forested grade, with the river itself as a reliable water source the whole way — top off here, since the route runs dry above. Some post-wildfire sections have significant blowdown; a few parties describe losing the tread briefly among downed timber and having to scramble back onto it. At ab…

name: Standard Scramble
approach: From the pullout along FR 6835 (West Fork Foss Road) — just past the concrete bridge over the East Fork Foss River, about half a mile from its junction with FR 68 and roughly 5.2 miles from US-2 at Skykomish — there is no maintained trail. Climbers cross to the north side of the road and pick up the toe of Bald Eagle's north ridge at about 1,600 ft, entering second-growth forest thick with fallen timber that requires weaving/scrambling over deadfall for the first few hundred feet of gain. Stay on or near the ridge crest heading south-southeast; around 2,600 ft the forest transitions to older g…
firstResearcherNote: A day scramble from the Foss River road with no camp on the north ridge; the car campground is the staging camp. Unsure whether the Bald Eagle Lake cirque lies on the north-ridge line, so it was dropped.

name: Northwest Couloir (Cedar Creek approach)
approach: From Highway 20 near Winthrop, reach the Cedar Creek Trailhead (reported at 2,961 ft elevation) and follow the Cedar Creek Trail before leaving it to bushwhack cross-country toward Cedar Creek; a known ford crossing (via a log in some years, a wade in others) gives access to the Shelokum Creek drainage, which is followed trail-less uphill to open meadows/snowfields below the northwest couloir.
firstResearcherNote: Cedar Creek side camps; unsure whether the meadow camps above the falls lie before the route leaves the trail.

camps.name: Cedar Creek meadow camps above the falls
camps.notes: The western approach camp, and the reason to use this side at all. Cedar Falls comes at about 1.7 miles from the trailhead and is the day-hike turnaround for most visitors; keep going and roughly two …

camps.name: Klipchuck Campground and the Highway 20 road-head campgrounds

name: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Cool Glacier)
approach: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (2,050 ft, end of Sloan Creek Road/FR 49), the North Fork Sauk River Trail (#649) climbs gently through old-growth forest. At about 2.1 miles pass the Pilot Ridge Trail junction (an alternate/bailout route), and by roughly 3.5 miles reach a crossing of Red Creek — a seasonal ford that can be a genuine early-season obstacle. About 1.5 miles beyond that is Mackinaw Shelter, the last reliable flat camping and water before the climb steepens; many parties camp here or push on. Past the shelter the trail switchbacks steeply for about 3 miles, gaining roughly…
firstResearcherNote: Cool/Gerdine Basin Camp has no notes; assumed to be a spot in the basin traverse between White Pass and Glacier Gap.

name: Southwest Route
approach: From Trinity Trailhead (end of Chiwawa River Road/FR-6200, about 23 miles up-road from WA-207 near Lake Wenatchee), three approaches reach Mount Berge's flanks within the Glacier Peak Wilderness. (1) Southwest approach: via the Little Giant Trail #1518, whose own trailhead sits at 2,600 ft about mile 19 of Chiwawa River Road; the trail climbs to Little Giant Pass (~10 mi round trip to the pass alone), drops into the Napeequa River valley, then follows a climbers' path upstream to the end of maintained tread at the creek draining Berge's southwest side. A steep, intermittent boot track then cli…
firstResearcherNote: Parties base at Buck Creek Pass or the High Pass camps; the route also lists a Little Giant approach whose exact camp is unclear, so the Napeequa camps were dropped.

name: Buckindy Glacier/Scramble Route
approach: From Darrington, drive north on SR 530 roughly 7-8 miles and turn right onto the Suiattle River Road (FR 26) just after crossing the Sauk River bridge. Follow FR 26 (pavement then gravel) about 20 miles, turn left onto FR 2680, and continue 6 miles to the Green Mountain Trailhead (~3,200 ft). Hike Green Mountain Trail #782 (about 4 miles, ~3,000 ft gain) through old growth and subalpine meadows to the lookout area, then go cross-country along the connecting ridge system east and southeast past the Horse Lake saddle, with slow sidehill travel toward Misch, to Buckindy's north slopes and glacier…
firstResearcherNote: Low confidence: the Green Mountain approach has first-night camps near Horse Lake saddle (added), but where parties base for the north-side route (Kindy head vs a basin west of Misch) is thinly documented.

name: Multi-Summit Scramble
approach: From I-90 Exit 34 (North Bend), drive Middle Fork Snoqualmie River Road (FR-56) east — paved at first, then good gravel — staying on FR-56 past the Taylor River Road (FR-5620) junction to a wide gravel wash / old borrow-pit pullout on the north side of the road near the base of the mountain (trailhead elevation roughly 1,150-1,200 ft). There is no maintained, numbered Forest Service trail here — this is an unmaintained climbers' boot path marked intermittently with cairns and pink flagging tape, not a hiking trail. From the wash, follow the dry creekbed/streambed uphill for roughly a mile; a b…
firstResearcherNote: Normally a long day from the road; unsure whether the East Peak line via Green Ridge Lake is part of this multi-summit route, so that lake was dropped.

name: Hester Lake Route
approach: Drive the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FR 56) to the Dingford Creek Trailhead (~1,400 ft). Hike the Dingford Creek Trail, crossing several creeks, toward the Hester Lake basin (roughly 5-6 miles) before leaving the trail to begin the off-trail scramble.
firstResearcherNote: Hester Lake is the documented overnight for Price; the Dingford roadside pull-outs are kept as the trailhead option but current dispersed-camping rules there are unclear.

name: Fire on the Mountain
approach: From the Mountain Loop Highway, turn onto FR 4096 (Bedal Creek Trailhead spur) and park at the trailhead, 2,790–2,800 ft. Follow the Bedal Creek Trail #705 through old-growth forest along Bedal Creek's steep banks; the maintained tread peters out roughly 1.5–2.5 miles in, at a large brushy washout coming down off the basin below Sloan's West Face. Scramble up the boulder- and blowdown-choked washout — this is the crux of route-finding on the approach — until a cairn marks an exit onto a climber's path (often flagged with pink tape) that switchbacks steeply through forest from about 3,500 ft to…
firstResearcherNote: Done in a big day or with a bivy at the base with running water; bivy elevation not confirmed so omitted.

name: Northeast Ridge (Nason Ridge Traverse)
approach: Begin at the Old Merritt Lake Trailhead off US-2 (~2,950 ft). Climb via Mahar Creek Ridge to Merritt Lake, then continue over Mt. Mastiff's Southeast Ridge and Mt. Howard's Northeast Ridge (both reported as snow climbs/rock scrambles) before dropping to the Howard-Rock col and climbing Rock Mountain's northeast side.
firstResearcherNote: Traverse Merritt-Mastiff-Howard-Rock; Crescent Lake is the midpoint camp, Rock Lake assumed on the descent via the Rock Mountain trail.

name: Southeast Slopes (Standard Scramble)
approach: The Southeast Slopes route is approached via the Upper Dungeness/Maynard Burn trail system, not by any direct road-side access - the drive only gets you to the trailhead at the end of FR-2860-120 (off FR-2870/Lost Mountain Rd, itself off Palo Alto Rd south of US-101 near Sequim). From the trailhead, the Lower Maynard Burn Trail #816 crosses Mueller Creek right away (the last easy, reliable water for a while) and follows an old roadbed before narrowing to single-track around 0.3 mile in. From there the trail turns and stays steep, gaining roughly 3,000 ft in a bit over 2 miles on tread that nar…
firstResearcherNote: Day route via Maynard Burn and Baldy; Cedar Lake is reached from the Gray Wolf River, a different approach, so it is dropped. Unsure whether parties camp on the ridge crest.

The first mile-plus is an easy, open ridge walk (the unmarked boot path up the Lillian Ridge Way / Elk Mountain high route splits off here for those doing the ridge-top variation instead). The trail then drops into the Grand Lake basin before climbing steadily to Grand Pass (6,488 ft) at roughly 5.95 mi and about 1,300 ft of net gain from the trailhe…

approach: From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 12.5 miles, turn left on Hannegan Pass Road (FR 32), continue just over a mile to the junction with Nooksack Cirque Road (FR 34), and follow FR 34 one mile to its end at the Nooksack Cirque Trailhead (do not confuse with the separate Hannegan Pass Trailhead further up FR 32). Ford Ruth Creek right at the trailhead — there is no bridge, and early-summer high water can make it difficult or unsafe to cross. Follow the old roadbed/Trail #750 up the North Fork Nooksack valley for roughly 50 minutes, then leave the trail and make an ascending…

name: South Route
approach: Ghost Peak sits deep in the Northern Pickets, just south of Crooked Thumb Peak and about 0.3 mi NNE of Phantom Peak, so this is a multi-day wilderness approach, not a day hike to a base. Standard access is from the Hannegan Pass Trailhead at the end of Ruth Creek Road (FR 32, ~3,100 ft) - not Ross Lake, which instead serves Luna Peak and Mount Fury further south via the Big Beaver Trail/Access Creek approach. From the Hannegan Trailhead, follow the Ruth Creek Trail over Hannegan Pass (5,066 ft, ~4 mi in) and drop into the Chilliwack River valley to a forest camp near Copper Creek/Graybeal Camp…

name: Luna Glacier
approach: Reaching Luna Cirque is the crux of the trip. The historical approach follows the Big Beaver Trail from Ross Lake (a $35 water taxi from Ross Lake Resort cuts about 6 miles off the hike) up to Luna Camp, then climbs steeply beside Luna Creek into the cirque — Fred Beckey himself described this bushwhack as 'the worst imaginable struggle with flies, devil's club, willows, and alder.' Most contemporary parties instead approach via Access Creek, which branches off that same Big Beaver Trail rather than a separate trailhead — parties continue on the maintained trail roughly 15-17.5 miles past Luna…

name: Southwest Route
approach: Mount Crowder has no trailhead and no maintained trail — every ascent is layered onto a multi-day, off-trail traverse through the heart of the Picket Range, and Crowder is almost never climbed as a standalone objective. Parties reach it via one of two corridors. From the south: the Goodell Creek climbers' path (turn off WA-20 opposite Newhalem into Goodell Creek Campground; the boot path starts behind a large boulder at the campground) climbs steeply and brushily through slide alder and old-growth timber, gaining roughly 2,500 ft in about a mile to reach the basins below McMillan Spire/Inspira…

approach: Drive WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the Ross Dam Trailhead (MP 134). Follow it roughly 11 miles to Luna Camp, then continue about 1.5 miles further to the Access Creek drainage; leave the trail and climb the brushy, moderately steep Access Creek valley (staying on its north side is recommended) to the open basin east of Luna Peak (~4,300 ft) — described as the easie…
